blocks.title: Class P
blocks.text: Class P is the set of problems a computer can solve efficiently, in polynomial time, by a deterministic algorithm (clear steps that always lead to the correct result).

Example: sorting [4, 1, 3, 2, 5] into [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. A computer can compare the first number with the second and swap them if needed, move to the next pair and repeat, and continue until the list is sorted. Going from 5 to 10 numbers increases the time, but it stays within a reasonable limit.

The book says doubling the list roughly doubles the time. That is exact only for a linear task: an O(n log n) sort takes a little more than double, and bubble sort, O(n^2), about four times; all of these are still polynomial.

blocks.prompt: Which complexity class represents problems solved efficiently by a deterministic algorithm (MCQ 2)?

items: P: solvable quickly (polynomial time) by clear deterministic steps; sorting is in P.
